title: Kristin Hannah Recommends 5 Books Perfect for Fall-From Twisty Thrillers to Historical Fiction - NewsBreak
text:
By Carissa Mosness ,
2 hours ago
With so many incredible books being published every week, it can be tough to decide what to read next. That’s why book recommendations are so important—and who better to suggest compelling, unputdownable reads than a beloved author who has written several best-selling books that are on so many readers’ best-book lists? We’ve rounded up some recommendations from Kristin Hannah . From small-town psychological thrillers to sweeping sagas spanning generations, her list of must-read books are perfect for fall’s shorter days and longer nights. Read on for her recommendations—you’ll want to add them all to your fall reading list ! And none of them are new releases, so they may be easier to find at your local library or bookstore!
‘The Push’ by Ashley Audrain
Penguin Books
In this Good Morning America book club pick, new mom Blythe Connor is determined to be the best mother to Violet. But in the exhausting early days of motherhood, Blythe is convinced that something is wrong with Violet. Her husband Fox thinks she's imagining it, but Blythe isn’t so sure, and her feelings don't change as the months pass by. Then, when their son Sam is born, Blythe bonds with him instantly—but after a devastating incident, Blythe's life turns upside down in seconds. Now she and her family are forced to face the truth of what happened to them, but nothing will prepare them for what they find.
What Kristin says : “Compulsively readable… A deep dive into the darkest nooks and crannies of motherhood. Raw, visceral, and often disturbing, this is an intense psychological drama that will be embraced by serious book clubs.”
What readers are saying: “ The Push makes us question the very nature of reality. Our protagonist vacillates between what she believes to be true and what she so desperately wants to deny. Her foundation has been ripped from under her feet and she no longer trusts her instincts. As readers, we struggle with trusting the narrator not because she wishes to deceive us but because she does not trust herself. The Push will haunt you long after the final sentence leaves you gasping.”
‘The Good Son’ by Jacquelyn Mitchard
MIRA
Filled with murder, mystery and a complex cast of characters, Jacquelyn Mitchard’s book is sure to stun. Stefan was just 17 when he went to prison for the murder of his girlfriend, Belinda. But he claims he doesn't remember what happened. After three years, he's released. Belinda’s mother refuses to make his return easy, while Stefan’s mother Thea, is determined to help her son live a normal life post-prison. But what happens when the son she loves turns out to be much more dangerous than she thought? A twisted story that will leave readers guessing.
What Kristin says : “Rich and complex, The Good Son is a compelling novel about the aftermath of a crime in a small, close-knit community.”
What readers are saying: “ The Good Son is a gripping suspenseful read. Thea is a woman willing to go to great lengths to protect her family. From the first chapter to the very last page this book held me hostage! The rich writing and descriptive details make for a lively book! You can't help but follow as Thea tries to find out the truth and protect her family at the same time. Wonderful read!
Kristin Hannah Shares Her Favorite Historical Fiction Reads
‘Loyalty’ by Lisa Scottoline
Putnam
This page-turning tale by bestselling author Lisa Scottoline transports readers to 1800s Sicily. Franco Fiorvanti is a handsome lemon grower with a dream: to own his own grove. He's willing to do whatever it takes to prove his worth to his powerful boss, Baron Zito. But when the Baron orders him to kidnap a young boy named Dante, Franco faces an impossible choice that sets off a chain of events that could change Sicily forever.
What Kristin says : “ Lisa Scottoline’s Loyalty is a gripping, compulsively readable tale of courage, loyalty, family secrets and the price of honor. An unputdownable piece of historical fiction that puts Scottoline’s talent for writing twisty plots and unforgettable characters on full display.”
What readers are saying: “The story has you transported 15 years after the kidnapping and each of these people play a special role in each other's lives as you will see that loyalty does come with a price. The ending is perfect. The author's note is wonderful, where things are explained between facts and fiction, and you learn so much.”
‘All the Sinners Bleed’ by S.A. Cosby
Flatiron Books
From bestselling author S.A. Cosby comes a terrifying murder mystery that will leave readers flipping pages long into the chilly fall nights. Titus Crown is the first Black sheriff in Charon County, Virginia, where there have only been two murders in the past couple of decades. But a year after Titus is elected, a school teacher is killed by a student and the student is shot by his deputies. As the investigation unfolds, Titus realizes there is a serial killer hiding in plain sight in the town. Elsewhere, some of the townspeople are hoping to have a parade in celebration of the town's Confederate history. Can Titus keep the drama at bay and catch the killer before he strike again?
What Kristin says : “A bold, raw new voice in the thriller landscape. All the Sinners Bleed has a dark, raw, Southern gothic noir feeling combined with a hard-edged look at the dark places in our past. Really enjoyed it.”
What readers are saying: “ All the Sinners Bleed is a five-star-plus read and one of the most powerful, unforgettable thrillers I’ve read. S.A. Cosby is operating at an elite level here. This story is dark, layered, emotionally heavy and absolutely gripping. The writing is razor-sharp, the tension is relentless and the characters feel painfully real. This book doesn’t just entertain, it confronts you. Every page carries weight, and the deeper you go, the more invested you become. I couldn’t put it down, and when it ended, it stayed with me.”
Ann Patchett's Favorite Historical Fiction Books
‘The Book of Fire’ by Christy Lefteri
Ballantine Books
Set in modern-day Greece, this novel follows Irini, a musician who teaches children to read and write, her husband Tasso, who paints pictures of the forest, and their daughter, Chara, after a devastating wildfire destroys their home. Months later, their village is trying to rebuild and Irini runs into the man who burned everything down. She is shocked to learn that he's dying and soon Irini makes a split-second choice that will haunt her forever. Elsewhere, Tasso, whose hands were badly burned in the fire, is trying to figure out how to paint again and looking for his father, who disappeared before the fire.
What Kristin says : “Uniquely crafted and full of both stunning imagery and human emotion… A story that will long remain in the reader’s mind.”
What readers are saying: “Told from two points in time, the novel chronicles both the timeline of the fire and of the woman's discovery of a dying man and her response to this death. Both timelines come together beautifully at the end. The pacing of the book was perfect, and I couldn't wait to pick up the storyline each day as I read it.”
